# llm

```go
import llm "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm"
```

Package llm holds what the llm.\* contracts share: a model reference, generated files, usage, model info, jobs and errors. It isn't a contract itself; llm.text/v1, llm.image/v1 and the others import it.

A model is named "provider/model": the name an app's admins gave a provider in Settings → LLM, a slash, and that provider's own id for the model ("vultr/glm-5.2", "or/z-ai/glm-5.2", "cf/@cf/black-forest-labs/flux-1-schnell"). It's split on the first slash. Every call names one: there are no defaults.

Source: [`ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/llm).

```go
const (
	UnitInputTokens  = "1M input tokens"
	UnitCachedTokens = "1M cached input tokens" // input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache
	UnitOutputTokens = "1M output tokens"       // reasoning tokens count as output
	// UnitTokens is input and output tokens together: the unit of a text model's measured price, since a call's bill
	// doesn't say how much was for input and how much for output.
	UnitTokens     = "1M tokens"
	UnitSecond     = "second" // of audio or video made (speech, music, video) or read (transcribe, align)
	UnitMegapixel  = "megapixel"
	UnitImage      = "image"
	UnitCharacters = "1K characters" // of text read aloud
	UnitRequest    = "request"       // one call, whatever it used
)
```

The units a Price is in. Every provider's prices are given in these, so prices compare across providers.

## Variables

<a id="errnotconfigured"></a><a id="errunknownmodel"></a><a id="errnotsupported"></a><a id="errprovider"></a><a id="errlimit"></a><a id="errtimeout"></a>

```go
var (
	ErrNotConfigured = &extkit.Error{Code: "not_configured", Status: 503,
		Message: "no providers yet: add one in Settings → LLM, then name a model as provider/model"}
	ErrUnknownModel = &extkit.Error{Code: "unknown_model", Status: 400,
		Message: "no such model: name one as provider/model from this kind's models list"}
	ErrNotSupported = &extkit.Error{Code: "not_supported", Status: 400, Message: "that provider doesn't do this"}
	ErrProvider     = &extkit.Error{Code: "provider", Status: 502, Message: "the provider answered with an error"}
	// ErrLimit: a limit in Settings → LLM refused the call before it reached the provider. Each refusal says which
	// limit and when its window resets ("try again after 00:00 UTC").
	ErrLimit = &extkit.Error{Code: "limit", Status: 429, Message: "a limit in Settings → LLM refused this call"}
	// ErrTimeout: the provider didn't answer in time and the request was cancelled. Its message names the model and
	// what ran out: a streamed answer that went quiet ("the provider sent nothing for 10s"), or the call's time limit
	// ("no answer in 3m0s"). Worth a retry, unlike a bad answer. A caller's own deadline or cancellation (a Go
	// context, an AbortSignal in page code) ends the call as that caller's error instead.
	ErrTimeout = &extkit.Error{Code: "timeout", Status: 504, Message: "the provider didn't answer in time"}
)
```

Errors every llm.\* contract may answer. A provider's own error comes back as ErrProvider's code with the cloud's status and message (never the key).


AllKinds lists every kind, in Settings → LLM's order.

### IsGuest

```go
func IsGuest(s string) bool
```

IsGuest reports whether s is an anonymous visitor's subject (by cookie or by IP).

### IsUser

```go
func IsUser(s string) bool
```

IsUser reports whether s is a signed-in auth record's subject.

### MicroUSD

```go
func MicroUSD(usd *float64) int64
```

MicroUSD is a cost in US dollars as millionths of a dollar, rounded to the nearest; nil is 0.

### OnCall

```go
func OnCall(app core.App) *hook.Hook[*CallEvent]
```

OnCall is the app's hook before every billable llm.\* call. A handler calls e.Next() to let the call go on, or returns e.Refuse(message) (or any error) to refuse it. A chain that doesn't reach its end refuses the call.

### OnCallDone

```go
func OnCallDone(app core.App) *hook.Hook[*CallDoneEvent]
```

OnCallDone is the app's hook after every llm.\* call that reached a provider. Its errors are logged; the call has already happened.

### SplitModel

```go
func SplitModel(ref string) (provider, model string, ok bool)
```

SplitModel splits "provider/model" on the first slash. ok is false without a slash or with an empty part.

```go
func SubjectOf(ctx context.Context) string
```

SubjectOf is the subject ctx carries, or "".


UserSubject is the subject for an auth record.

## Types

### CallDoneEvent

```go
type CallDoneEvent struct {
	hook.Event
	App     core.App
	Context context.Context

	Kind    string
	Op      string
	Model   string
	Subject string
	Usage   Usage
	Job     string // a job's id, for music and video
}
```

CallDoneEvent is a call that reached a provider, with what it used. A music or video job's comes once its cost is known (when it's done), or never for a job nobody checks again.

### CallEvent

```go
type CallEvent struct {
	hook.Event
	App     core.App
	Context context.Context

	Kind string // "text", "image", "speech", "transcribe", "align", "music", "video" or "embed"
	Op   string // the contract operation: "complete", "stream", "generate", "speak", ...
	// Model is the call's "provider/model"; a handler may change it.
	Model string
	// Subject is whom the call is for (see WithSubject): "user:<collection>/<id>", "guest:<id>",
	// "guest:ip:<address>", "" for nobody in particular, or any name a handler gives it ("team:acme").
	Subject string
	// Input is a pointer to the operation's input (*textv1.CompleteInput, *imagev1.GenerateInput, ...); a handler may
	// change its fields. Its model field is ignored: change Model.
	Input any
	// Auth is who made the call.
	Auth extkit.Auth
	// GuestsCapped says a handler takes care of what guests may spend, so the built-in limits don't refuse guest
	// calls for want of a limit on all guests together.
	GuestsCapped bool
}
```

CallEvent is one billable call on its way to a provider.

### CallEvent.Refuse

```go
func (e *CallEvent) Refuse(message string) error
```

Refuse returns the error that refuses the call with message, the way a used-up limit does (code "limit", 429). Return it from a handler instead of calling e.Next().

### ContentInput

```go
type ContentInput struct {
	ID    string `json:"id"`
	Index int    `json:"index,omitempty"`
}
```

ContentInput names one of a done job's files.

### Enrich

```go
type Enrich struct {
	Buckets []string `json:"buckets"`
	Limit   int      `json:"limit,omitempty"` // passages to add (default 5, at most 20)
	Query   string   `json:"query,omitempty"`
	// Viewer is who the answer is for: passages from records they can't view (the collection's view rule) are left
	// out. Nil sees everything, as the app's own server code.
	Viewer *Viewer `json:"viewer,omitempty"`
}
```

Enrich adds passages from the app's search buckets (search/v1) to a call's prompt: the call searches Buckets with Query (default: the prompt, or the last user message) and sends the best Limit passages after it. In JSON it's an object, or just the list of buckets (\["storytime"]).

### Enrich.UnmarshalJSON

```go
func (e *Enrich) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error
```

UnmarshalJSON takes the object form or a list of bucket names.

### File

```go
type File struct {
	Name string `json:"name,omitempty"`
	Type string `json:"type,omitempty"` // a media type: image/png, audio/mpeg, video/mp4
	Data []byte `json:"data,omitempty"`
	URL  string `json:"url,omitempty"`
}
```

File is generated media, or media sent in (audio to transcribe, an image to edit). Data is the bytes (base64 over HTTP); URL is the provider's hosted copy when it gave one, which may expire. Name is a suggested file name.

### Job

```go
type Job struct {
	ID       string  `json:"id"`
	Status   string  `json:"status"` // queued, running, done or failed
	Progress float64 `json:"progress,omitempty"`
	Files    []File  `json:"files,omitempty"`
	// Outputs is how many files the job made, for content's index (0..Outputs-1), once it's done.
	Outputs int    `json:"outputs,omitempty"`
	Error   string `json:"error,omitempty"`
	Model   string `json:"model"`
	Usage   Usage  `json:"usage"`
}
```

Job is a long generation (music, video): started by create, followed by get, its files fetched by content. The id carries the provider ("vultr:music\_02a2..."), so get and content find it again. Files are filled in once it's done when the provider returns them inline or create was given wait.

JobRef names a job, for get.

### ModelInfo

```go
type ModelInfo struct {
	ID       string   `json:"id"`       // "provider/model", what a call names
	Provider string   `json:"provider"` // the provider's name in Settings → LLM
	Type     string   `json:"type"`     // the provider's type: vultr, cloudflare, openrouter, openai
	Name     string   `json:"name,omitempty"`
	Kinds    []string `json:"kinds"`
	Inputs   []string `json:"inputs,omitempty"` // what it reads: text, image, audio...
	// Reasoning is true for a model that thinks before answering (its thinking counts toward maxTokens).
	Reasoning     bool `json:"reasoning,omitempty"`
	ContextTokens int  `json:"contextTokens,omitempty"`
	// Prices are its listed prices, then the prices measured from this app's own calls, each marked by Source. None
	// means its price isn't known.
	Prices      []Price `json:"prices,omitempty"`
	Description string  `json:"description,omitempty"`
	// Size is how many parameters it has, as its maker names it: "1.7B", "27B", "30B (3B active)" for a
	// mixture of experts.
	Size string `json:"size,omitempty"`
	// Features are what it can do beyond its kind, from the Feature constants.
	Features []string `json:"features,omitempty"`
	// Languages are the languages it speaks, writes or hears (ISO 639-1 codes), when the provider lists them.
	Languages []string `json:"languages,omitempty"`
}
```

ModelInfo is one model, as each contract's models operation lists it. Every field past Kinds is optional: a provider fills what it says about the model, and nothing is guessed.

### Options

```go
type Options = map[string]any
```

Options are a provider's own fields, passed through unchanged (seed, steps, aspect\_ratio, OpenRouter's provider routing...). They override what the contract's fields set.

### Passage

```go
type Passage struct {
	Bucket   string  `json:"bucket"`
	Source   string  `json:"source,omitempty"`
	Document string  `json:"document"`
	Heading  string  `json:"heading,omitempty"`
	Text     string  `json:"text"`

```

Passage is a piece of a search bucket that was added to a prompt, and where it came from.

### Price

```go
type Price struct {
	Unit string  `json:"unit"`
	USD  float64 `json:"usd"`
	// Source is where the price comes from: "listed" (the provider's own model list; also when empty) or "measured"
	// (what this app's calls to the model were billed, from the ledger: cost divided by what they used).
	Source string `json:"source,omitempty"`
	// Calls is, for a measured price, how many billed calls it was measured over.
	Calls int `json:"calls,omitempty"`
}
```

Price is one of a model's prices: USD per Unit, one of the Unit constants. A price is a rate on one meter of a call; a model may list several (input and output tokens), and a call's cost is each meter's use times its rate, added up.

### SubjectParts

```go
type SubjectParts struct {
	Kind       string `json:"kind"`                 // "user", "guest", "" (nobody), or a custom subject's prefix
	Collection string `json:"collection,omitempty"` // a user's auth collection
	ID         string `json:"id,omitempty"`         // a user's record id, a guest's cookie id, or what follows a custom prefix
	IP         string `json:"ip,omitempty"`         // a guest counted by IP
}
```

SubjectParts is a subject taken apart.

### ParseSubject

```go
func ParseSubject(s string) SubjectParts
```

ParseSubject takes a subject apart: "user:users/abc" is {user, users, abc}, "guest:ip:10.0.0.1" is {guest, ip 10.0.0.1}, "team:acme" is {team, acme}.

### Usage

```go
type Usage struct {
	InputTokens     int     `json:"inputTokens,omitempty"`
	OutputTokens    int     `json:"outputTokens,omitempty"`
	CachedTokens    int     `json:"cachedTokens,omitempty"`    // input tokens that came from the provider's prompt cache
	ReasoningTokens int     `json:"reasoningTokens,omitempty"` // output tokens the model spent thinking
	Seconds         float64 `json:"seconds,omitempty"`         // audio or video length billed
	// CostMicroUSD is what the call cost, in millionths of a US dollar (1,000,000 is $1; 1,000 is a tenth of a cent),
	// as a whole number so costs add up exactly. It's what the provider charged when it says (OpenRouter on every call,
	// Vultr for media), else an estimate from the model's listed prices and what the call used (CostEstimated), else 0:
	// 0 means free or not known.
	CostMicroUSD int64 `json:"costMicroUSD"`
	// CostEstimated is true when CostMicroUSD was worked out from listed prices rather than reported by the provider.
	CostEstimated bool `json:"costEstimated,omitempty"`
}
```

Usage is what a call used. The token and seconds fields appear only when known; CostMicroUSD is always there. Every llm.\* contract's reply carries one (chat's in its answer, music's and video's on the job).

### Viewer

```go
type Viewer struct {
	Collection string `json:"collection,omitempty"`
	ID         string `json:"id,omitempty"`
}
```

Viewer is a signed-in auth record (Collection and ID), or a guest (both empty).
